title: Second rule — rites only God could institute, absent from Scripture, must be Apostolic
source_text: XVII. Secunda regula nitens iisdem fundamentis haec est, Quod ea quae servat Ecclesia Romana quae sunt ejusmodi, ut nemo nisi Deus legitime potuerit illa instituere, nec tamen in Scripturis reperiuntur a Deo instituta, ab Apostolis tradita fuisse necesse sit.
pass_a_gloss: The second rule, resting on the same foundations, is this: that those things which the Roman Church keeps which are of such a kind that no one but God could lawfully have instituted them, and yet are not found in the Scriptures as instituted by God, must necessarily have been handed down by the Apostles.
pass_b_english: Second rule, on the same two foundations: what Rome keeps that only God could lawfully institute, yet Scripture never shows God instituting, must have come from the Apostles.

lemmas.latin: nemo nisi Deus legitime potuerit illa instituere
lemmas.gloss: no one but God could lawfully have instituted them

lemmas.latin: ab Apostolis tradita fuisse necesse sit
lemmas.gloss: must necessarily have been handed down by the Apostles

choices.why: Marks divine right to institute, not mere custom.
Forced inference from the two foundations.
